My land here in Quzhou has always grown wheat and corn. My husband farmed it the same way before he passed, and his father before him. I know this land. I know when the soil is ready and when it needs water. Books — I never needed them for this.

I have about 8 mu. It is not much, but it is mine. This year I will do what I always do: plant wheat in October after the corn comes off, and corn again in June after the wheat harvest. The same land, both crops, every year. My neighbors do it too. If I tried something different and it failed, I would have nothing to eat and no money to show my son.

For seeds, I will buy from the village supply cooperative — whatever improved wheat variety they are selling this year. I do not know the name, I just ask the man there what other people are buying. For corn, hybrid seed. Everyone uses hybrid now. It grows better.

Fertilizer: I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then urea when the wheat starts to grow tall. I do the same amount I did last year — maybe a bag more on the corn because last year the leaves looked a little yellow. I do not measure exactly. I know roughly how many bags per mu from years of doing it.

Water: wheat needs water in winter to get through the freeze, then again when it joints and when it heads. Three times at least, maybe four if it is dry. Corn I water once or twice — usually once at planting if the ground is dry, and once when it silks.

I will spray for aphids on the wheat like I always do in spring, and once on the corn for borer. Nothing more unless I see a problem.

I do rotary tillage. My son comes back to help with the machine before planting. Ploughing deep is too hard now — my back cannot take it and hiring someone costs too much.
